title: Screening millions of well records with geospatial machine learning
summary: I developed a geospatial machine-learning workflow to identify likely orphaned-well candidates within a national inventory of roughly 7–8 million records. Basin-specific XGBoost models, training-based threshold selection and SHAP analysis exposed regional differences and informed a separate Appalachian experiment using additional Enverus attributes.
role: Geospatial data scientist · Label reconciliation, feature engineering and modeling

image.alt: Out-of-fold precision recall and F1 threshold curves for Appalachian
image.caption: Appalachian — training out-of-fold precision, recall and F1 versus decision threshold. The selected threshold was chosen using training data.

problem: A national well inventory contained incomplete and inconsistent reporting, while orphaned-well prevalence and record quality differed across regions. Researchers needed a screening method that could prioritize candidate wells for further review and expose where model performance was uncertain.
contribution: Starting from a national inventory assembled by another team, I reconciled state-specific known-orphan records and identifiers, engineered predictive features, and developed the national and basin-specific modeling workflows. I tuned XGBoost, selected decision thresholds, evaluated regional performance and produced SHAP summaries, then investigated an Enverus-enriched Appalachian model.

approach.title: Reconcile labels before modeling
approach.body: Queried state records and identifiers to associate known-orphan labels with the broader well inventory. Standardized dates and categories while handling missing or inconsistent attributes.

approach.title: Engineer operational and spatial features
approach.body: Used well type, dates, state, depth, land cover and location. A haversine BallTree calculated distance to known orphans using a training-partition reference inventory, with additional distance and missingness features.

approach.title: Adapt the model to regional differences
approach.body: After exploring logistic regression and Random Forest, focused on XGBoost and separate eligible basin models. A stratified 70/30 split retained holdout records; basin-specific cross-validation used three or five folds.

approach.title: Tune probabilities and thresholds separately
approach.body: Used BayesSearchCV to tune XGBoost for average precision, then out-of-fold training predictions to select an F1-based threshold. Holdout evaluation included precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC and PR-AUC.

approach.title: Inspect errors and extend the strongest data context
approach.body: Used SHAP to examine feature contributions and compared metrics with positive-class support. The regional variability motivated a separate Appalachian enrichment study in an approximately 900,000-well universe with uneven Enverus coverage.

outcome: Historical reports document substantial differences among basins. In the March baseline, Appalachian precision and recall were 68.0% and 61.2%; Fort Worth recall was 28.1% on only 32 positive holdout records. Those differences helped direct the next analysis toward regional data enrichment instead of relying on a single national score.
learning: The documented progression runs from label reconciliation and baseline comparisons to regional modeling, threshold decisions and targeted data enrichment. It demonstrates adaptation to the evidence: performance is assessed against class prevalence, available attributes and the intended review task, with model interpretation used to guide the next investigation.
limitations: The underlying research inventory is not public. Historical figures and metrics are preserved outputs, not results reproduced during this portfolio update.

The March baseline reports, earlier presentation checkpoint and later Enverus-enriched Appalachian work are separate snapshots. A complete numerical comparison for the enriched model is not available here.

Very high precision and small positive-class samples require independent validation and checks for duplicate records, spatial dependence and feature leakage. The reports alone neither prove nor rule out overfitting.
Training-only nearest-orphan references exclude the holdout, but preprocessing and label-derived features still require fold-specific leakage review before the historical script is reused.
Predictions support candidate screening. They do not determine legal orphan status, establish contamination or measure methane emissions.

evidence.title: March baseline: all 11 basin reports
evidence.body: Class 1 precision, recall, F1 and positive support are transcribed from the original March _HC classification reports. Percentages are rounded as displayed. These are basin holdout results, not the enriched Appalachian model or the earlier presentation checkpoint.

evidence.title: Training-based decision thresholds
evidence.body: Eleven original out-of-fold training curves show precision, recall and F1 as the threshold changes. Threshold selection occurred on training predictions before holdout evaluation.

evidence.title: Why precision was not enough
evidence.body: The reported Permian holdout contained 184 positive records among 175,286 wells; Western Gulf contained 546 among 181,806. These prevalence differences, and Fort Worth’s 32 positive cases, make recall, F1 and support essential context for headline precision.
